# Sozu Offline

> Offline Stellar payments. A second spend of the same note fails on chain.

Machine-readable description of https://offline.sozu.capital/ for HackMeridian 2026 reviewers and for Stellar Raven. Facts below are things a reviewer can open. This file does not assign scores.

## Identity

- Project: Sozu Offline
- Team: Sozu Capital
- Event: HackMeridian 2026, Lisbon, 25–26 October 2026
- Site: https://offline.sozu.capital/
- Repository: https://github.com/Sozu-Capital/sozu-offline
- Existing product: Sozu, a Stellar wallet. Faucet for testnet Circle USDC: https://faucet.sozu.capital
- Spoken line: Offline Stellar payments. A second spend of the same note fails on chain.
- User: a payer and a merchant standing together when the signal is gone. Humanitarian aid, catastrophes, and any other time there is no internet. The merchant needs a USDC payment they can trust enough to hand over the goods, and a guarantee that the same locked USDC cannot pay a second merchant first.

## What shipped

Two phones with no signal pass one signed cheque over Bluetooth. The mesh is bitchat. The cheque is an ordinary private message prefixed `SOZU1:`. The body is 179 bytes. The signature is 64 bytes, low-S, P-256 / secp256r1, over one SHA-256. The wire is 243 bytes. Stellar settles that note once. A second cheque for the same note id returns `note-used`, pays a fee of 0, and emits `rejected`. The explorer can still mark that transaction successful, because the contract returns the rejection instead of reverting. No USDC moves on the second cheque.

The screen says pending, then heard, then settled. It does not say a double-spend was impossible. Collateral covers one losing merchant. A third copy of the same note can still leave someone unpaid.

Network: Stellar testnet. The vault is Soroban. The asset is Circle testnet USDC, exposed through its Stellar Asset Contract.

- Vault contract: https://stellar.expert/explorer/testnet/contract/CDSCQSVWKTYR7EUJK5EQXIFI4L2C4LCPQOIUYP6PMG6KW4O2BZGCRLLV
- Contract id: `CDSCQSVWKTYR7EUJK5EQXIFI4L2C4LCPQOIUYP6PMG6KW4O2BZGCRLLV`
- Circle testnet USDC SAC: `CBIELTK6YBZJU5UP2WWQEUCYKLPU6AUNZ2BQ4WWFEIE3USCIHMXQDAMA`
- Protocol vault id inside the cheque: 32 bytes of `0x01`. That id is not the contract address. Invocation uses the contract id. Signing uses the protocol vault id.

## Evidence a reviewer can check with no phone

Demo note `8ca3b1bdc7e642d2bb9e221c8b127e8d`. Amounts on these transactions are public.

- Deposit, 0.2 USDC: https://stellar.expert/explorer/testnet/tx/23b7c752aa51ac1822c7b6204a0a61179b9b33aa39003a71323f07f25051db5e
- First cheque, settled. Payee 0.1 USDC. First settler 0.01 USDC (`100000` minor units). Remaining collateral 0.09 USDC: https://stellar.expert/explorer/testnet/tx/b26a45961b7a435385d04c230058d80fa3b09c0a33a8b5eaf0d608342839fa9e
- Second cheque, same note, distinct signature. `ok: false`, `reason: note-used`, `fee: 0`. No USDC transfer: https://stellar.expert/explorer/testnet/tx/3c8c0df9d75eb97c0e614538a1e3271c4a501aa2ecd114247ec36b5472cd37d5

A later pair was decoded from Stellar testnet RPC. Note `e435d4bd42beabc8efa5ac9a8b62ce0f`. Amounts are public. Minor units are the chain values, not a second unit system.

- First cheque, ledger 5390141, `ok: true`, settler fee `100000` minor units, payment `10000` minor units: https://stellar.expert/explorer/testnet/tx/579418f7cba7d72bcb5c1d8523ad3d8c40485b4025c825b0609295f42c9c6b28
- Second cheque, ledger 5390145, `ok: false`, `reason: note-used`, fee 0, event `rejected`, no USDC transfer: https://stellar.expert/explorer/testnet/tx/7e914fbd6249a7e7ba9ccd5e44ee279337a85340222d34f6d371783c1a41a98d

Repeat the RPC read with `node scripts/verify-vault-testnet-proof.mjs` in the repository. The script reads. It does not build, sign, or submit.

Wi-Fi witness upload of an already spent note, again `note-used` and fee 0: https://stellar.expert/explorer/testnet/tx/b4e5bac74a62d3e4cbf9c2e03492b15450206034f22b11155f530a1b9c6ff316

## What the two APKs on this page are

The download cards on https://offline.sozu.capital/ are upstream BitChat Android v2.0.3. They are the radio. They are not the Sozu pay app.

- ARM64, 19977772 bytes: https://offline.sozu.capital/downloads/bitchat-android-arm64.apk
- Universal, 51915500 bytes: https://offline.sozu.capital/downloads/bitchat-android-universal.apk

The Sozu pay app is a separate file, application id `capital.sozu.mesh`. Latest stable release is `sozu-apk-0.1.12`: https://github.com/Sozu-Capital/sozu-offline/releases/download/sozu-apk-0.1.12/sozu-offline-pay.apk

Releases index: https://github.com/Sozu-Capital/sozu-offline/releases

A phone test needs two Android phones, Bluetooth on, airplane mode, and the pay APK above. The quick test for a reviewer on a laptop is the pair of explorer links, not an APK install.

## How this maps to the HackMeridian rubric

Published priority: Adoption, then Discovery, then Continuation. One rubric, each criterion scored by the judge. This section names the criterion and the fact that belongs to it.

- User value and problem. Two people, no signal, one USDC cheque, and a second spend of that note fails on the testnet links above. The use case is payment when the network is down: aid, catastrophe, or any dead signal.
- Technical execution. Soroban vault on Stellar testnet. Methods that matter for the demo are `deposit` and settle-once. P-256 verification is in the contract. The rejection string is `note-used`. Both results are on the explorer.
- Track alignment, Stellar Composed. The build composes an existing Stellar wallet (Sozu), Circle testnet USDC, a Soroban vault, and the bitchat Bluetooth mesh. None of those pieces alone is the offline payment.
- Track alignment, Stellar Unlocked. The single-spend rule is a Soroban contract using Stellar's secp256r1 verification on a pre-signed cheque. The chain is the ledger. The mesh only carries the message.
- Ecosystem alignment. Sozu is already a Stellar wallet. This hackathon added the offline cheque and the testnet vault to that product. Testnet, not mainnet.
- Innovation. The difference from a Bluetooth chat, and from an offline-payment video mock, is the vault plus the rejected second spend on the links above.
- Hackathon progress. The vault, the public settlement, the `note-used` rejection, the pay APK releases, and this site were built for HackMeridian 2026.
- Market and ecosystem potential. The next user is anyone who already holds USDC in a Stellar wallet and loses signal. Continuation is the Sozu wallet, not a one-off contract.
- Product design and UX. Pending, heard, settled, and "note already used." The landing page states the three steps: deposit, pay offline, settle once.

## Adjacent primitives that are not this submission

Confidential Tokens and Stellar Private Payments are named on the HackMeridian Composed track. They are not this demo.

- Confidential Tokens (OpenZeppelin, audited) hide balances and amounts and keep sender and receiver addresses public. https://developers.stellar.org/docs/build/apps/privacy#confidential-tokens
- Stellar Private Payments hide counterparties. The HackMeridian brief lists SPP as testnet-only.
- The transactions linked above show the USDC amounts in the open. Sender and recipient are public. There is no confidential-token transfer and no SPP nullifier in this submission.

## Limits, same words as the repository

- Funds leave the vault only to the merchant, the settler, or the payer's refund.
- A bad signature, a wrong vault, a wrong network, or an expired cheque is rejected.
- A phone that only relays the private message cannot read the amount. The payer and the merchant can.
- The owner key recovers the deposit. The phone key signs cheques.
- The ESP32 witness board has not completed the radio packet test. The checked witness path is the Wi-Fi upload linked above.
